questions.question: What is Marshall University's athletic nickname?
questions.explanation: Marshall's teams are the Thundering Herd. The Mountaineers are rival WVU.
questions.tidbit: Marshall's school colors are kelly green and white.

questions.question: Which 2006 movie tells the story of Marshall football's rebuild after the 1970 plane crash?
questions.explanation: We Are Marshall starred Matthew McConaughey as head coach Jack Lengyel.
questions.tidbit: Matthew Fox played assistant coach Red Dawson, who drove home from a recruiting trip instead of taking the flight.

questions.question: Marshall University's main campus is in which West Virginia city?
questions.explanation: Marshall is in Huntington, on the Ohio River. Morgantown is home to WVU.
questions.tidbit: Huntington is named for railroad magnate Collis P. Huntington, who founded it as a Chesapeake & Ohio Railway terminus.

questions.question: What is the name of Marshall's bison mascot?
questions.explanation: The costumed bison mascot is Marco.
questions.tidbit: Marshall plays home football games at Joan C. Edwards Stadium.

questions.question: Marshall University is named after which person?
questions.explanation: The school began in 1837 as Marshall Academy, named for Chief Justice John Marshall.
questions.tidbit: John Marshall served as Chief Justice from 1801 to 1835, the longest tenure of any chief justice.

questions.question: Southern Airways Flight 932 crashed near Huntington on November 14, 1970, with the Marshall football team aboard. How many people died?
questions.explanation: All 75 people aboard were killed: players, coaches, staff, boosters and the flight crew.
questions.tidbit: Every November 14 the Memorial Fountain on campus is turned off. It stays silent until spring.

questions.question: What is the name of the Reds' home ballpark, opened in 2003?
questions.explanation: Great American Ball Park replaced Riverfront Stadium (later Cinergy Field). Crosley Field came before that.
questions.tidbit: The riverboat-style smokestacks beyond center field shoot fireworks when a Red hits a home run.

questions.question: The 1869 Cincinnati Red Stockings are famous for being...
options: The first openly all-professional baseball team
The first team to play a night game
The first team to wear numbers
questions.explanation: The 1869 Red Stockings were the first openly all-professional team, paying every player.
questions.tidbit: They went unbeaten through the entire 1869 season.

questions.question: Who managed the Big Red Machine to World Series titles in 1975 and 1976?
questions.explanation: Sparky Anderson. Lou Piniella managed the 1990 title team.
questions.tidbit: Anderson's nickname was "Captain Hook" because he pulled starting pitchers so quickly.

questions.question: Pete Rose finished his career as MLB's all-time hits leader. How many hits?
questions.explanation: 4,256 hits. He passed Ty Cobb in 1985.
questions.tidbit: Rose also holds the MLB record for most games played: 3,562.

questions.question: In the 1990 World Series, the Reds swept which team?
questions.explanation: They swept the heavily favored Oakland A's. Pittsburgh was their NLCS opponent.
questions.tidbit: Pitcher Jose Rijo was named World Series MVP.

questions.question: In 1938, Reds pitcher Johnny Vander Meer did something no other MLB pitcher has done. What?
options: Threw a World Series perfect game
questions.explanation: Vander Meer threw consecutive no-hitters, on June 11 and June 15, 1938.
questions.tidbit: The second one came in the first night game ever played at Brooklyn's Ebbets Field.

questions.question: This number is retired by every Major League Baseball team. Who does it honor?
questions.explanation: MLB retired 42 league-wide in 1997, 50 years after Jackie Robinson broke baseball's color barrier.
questions.tidbit: Every player in the majors wears 42 on April 15, Jackie Robinson Day.

questions.question: This number is retired across an entire pro league. Which league?
questions.explanation: The NHL retired 99 for every team in 2000 to honor Wayne Gretzky.
questions.tidbit: Gretzky picked 99 as a junior player because his hero Gordie Howe's 9 was already taken.

questions.question: In 2022 the NBA retired one number for every team, honoring Bill Russell. Which number?
questions.explanation: Russell wore 6 for the Celtics. It was the first number retired across the whole NBA.
questions.tidbit: Russell won 11 NBA championships in his 13 seasons.

questions.question: On February 14, 1990, in Orlando, Michael Jordan's jersey was stolen. What number did he wear instead?
questions.explanation: He wore a spare number 12 with no name on the back. He wore 45 in his 1995 comeback and 9 at the Olympics.
questions.tidbit: He still scored 49 points that night.

questions.question: Which animal is on Lamborghini's badge?
questions.explanation: A charging bull. The prancing horse is Ferrari and the scorpion is Abarth.
questions.tidbit: Many Lamborghini models are named after famous fighting bulls, including the Murcielago and the Aventador.

questions.question: Before building supercars, Ferruccio Lamborghini made his fortune building...
questions.explanation: His tractor company, Lamborghini Trattori, came first. The car company followed in 1963.
questions.tidbit: The story goes that he started building cars after Enzo Ferrari brushed off his complaints about a Ferrari clutch.

questions.question: Koenigsegg builds its hypercars in the country with this flag. Which country?
questions.explanation: Sweden. Koenigsegg is based in Angelholm.
questions.tidbit: The factory sits on a former Swedish Air Force fighter base, and the cars carry the old squadron's ghost emblem.

questions.question: The McLaren F1 seats three people. Where does the driver sit?
options: In the center, ahead of the passengers
questions.explanation: The driver sits in the middle, slightly forward, with a passenger seat set back on each side.
questions.tidbit: In 1998 it hit 240.1 mph, making it the fastest production car in the world at the time.

questions.question: Bugatti is headquartered in Molsheim. Which country is that in?
questions.explanation: Molsheim is in Alsace, France, where Ettore Bugatti founded the company in 1909.
questions.tidbit: Since 2021 Bugatti has been part of Bugatti Rimac, a joint venture with Croatia's Rimac and Porsche.

questions.question: Ferrari's prancing horse first appeared on the plane of which World War I flying ace?
questions.explanation: Italian ace Francesco Baracca. His mother suggested Enzo Ferrari use the horse for luck.
questions.tidbit: The yellow background behind the horse is the color of Modena, Enzo Ferrari's hometown.
